problem: He did not know the licence had to be displayed
action: Inside the office. The dealer stands facing a bare wall, looking up at it. The wall carries four or five empty picture frames and a couple of bare nails and hooks where documents should be displayed — every frame is empty, holding nothing but plain backing card. His hands hang at his sides. He is just looking at the emptiness.
lighting: Flat indoor daylight from a window off to one side, the wall evenly lit and slightly grubby. Ordinary, unglamorous light.
camera: From behind and slightly to the side, over his shoulder — he occupies the lower left of the vertical frame, seen three-quarter from behind, with the empty frames on the wall filling the upper right. Sharp throughout. 35mm.
detail: CRITICAL — every frame on the wall is completely EMPTY. No certificates, no paper, no documents, no text, no letters, no numbers, no printing, no logos, nothing behind the glass. Just blank backing. Same cream full-sleeve shirt with the sleeves rolled, same dark navy trousers, same watch.
feeling: Standing in front of the thing you were supposed to have done, that nobody ever told you about.
motion: He lifts his hand halfway towards one empty frame and lets it fall again. A slow push in. Nothing else moves, no cuts, no camera shake, nobody speaks.

voice_over.hi: ट्रेड लाइसेंस लगाना भी ज़रूरी है। ये तो मुझे पता ही नहीं था।
